According to the theory of special relativity, length contraction is given by the formula:
$$L = L_0 \sqrt{1 - \frac{v^2}{c^2}}$$
where:
- $L_0 = 5\text{ m}$ (proper length)
- $v = 0.8c$ (velocity of the rod)
- $c$ = speed of light

Substitute the values into the formula:
$$L = 5 \sqrt{1 - \frac{(0.8c)^2}{c^2}}$$
$$L = 5 \sqrt{1 - 0.64}$$
$$L = 5 \sqrt{0.36}$$
$$L = 5 \times 0.6 = 3\text{ m}$$

**Answer:**
The length of the rod when moving at $0.8c$ is **$3\text{ m}$**.
proTip: Length contraction occurs only along the direction of motion; dimensions perpendicular to the motion remain unchanged.
